TWO_DEFECTS_THE_COORDINATOR_FOUND_THAT_T: (1) THE PUBLISHED SPEARMAN WAS WRONG AND WORSE THAN WRONG. np.argsort(np.argsort(x)) gives ORDINAL ranks, breaking ties by position; with widths {48,64,96} over nine cells the five 64s took five distinct ranks instead of midranks. I computed the correct value TWO WAYS BEFORE SAYING ANYTHING - my own midrank implementation and scipy.stats.spearmanr, both 0.5809475019311126 against the published 0.5333333333333333. THEN THE AGENT FOUND WORSE THAN I HAD: the old expression was NOT WELL DEFINED, because its arrays came from a groupby().median() so rows arrived alphabetically giving 0.5333, while THE SAME EXPRESSION ON THE SAME DATA IN EXECUTION ORDER GIVES 0.8499999999999999. I verified both to every digit. The midrank form is invariant at 0.5809475019311126. The finding was unchanged in direction and STRENGTHENED in magnitude. (2) An agent-reported 1173 passed / 0 failures became 1 failed / 1193 passed under my own run - which is why an agent's self-reported test count is never entered into a tracker.
WHERE_THE_COORDINATOR_WAS_WRONG_AND_THE_: I diagnosed the ordering flake as an OVERFLOW at [3.0,2.0] x 1e308. The counterexample is real and I verified it, BUT IT CANNOT HAVE BEEN THE DRAW THAT FAILED: the file's strategies cap values and factors at 1e6, which I then confirmed by reading them. The agent found the reachable route - an ordinary ROUNDING COLLISION at [-811260.5389416472, 1000000.0, 999999.9999999999] x 292915.2677047961, two values one ulp apart whose products round together, nothing overflowing - and I reproduced it: ordering [0,2,1] becomes [0,1,2]. My CLASS was right and the fix I specified covers it; my MECHANISM was wrong. Last night's lesson was that a coordinator re-using an agent's number as its own cross-check has stopped cross-checking; the converse is that a coordinator dressing a plausible guess as a finding has done the same thing in the other direction. ON THE SECOND FAILURE I DID BETTER: I handed the agent the hypothesis I had RULED OUT - 400 bootstrap trials showing the point median outside its interval in 0 of 400 for four stages, so quantisation was not the cause - and let it find the mechanism.

CARRY_OVER_NEW_TONIGHT: (1) A GREEN RELEASE GATE IS ONE SAMPLE. Two runs disagreed on byte-identical content. Any future session that publishes on a single gate run is publishing on a sample of one, and P100 now gives the bound: a clean two-run check is consistent with a defect rate as high as 0.776. Run the gate twice before publishing, or state that you did not. (2) A TIMING PRODUCT'S VALIDATION MUST NOT ASSERT TIMING RELATIONSHIPS ON A SHARED RUNNER. Five intermittent failures and a sixth caught in flight all trace to checks comparing wall-clock measurements. Reduce every such check to a direction or a bound with measured bands published. (3) A VALIDATION SCRIPT MUST NEVER REGENERATE EVIDENCE ANOTHER ONE PINS. The gate runs sorted(glob('*.py')), so adjacent scripts run back to back; P100's audit overwrote the file its sibling pinned and the gate's own ordering guaranteed the collision. Campaigns belong in data/, with their output committed and hashed. (4) A PROBE THAT RE-RUNS VALIDATION SCRIPTS MUST REDIRECT THEIR OUTPUT. P094's working-directory probe silently replaced all twelve committed outputs with reduced runs, so the committed evidence was no longer what the document quoted. (5) CHECK WHETHER A COUNTEREXAMPLE IS REACHABLE BEFORE CALLING IT THE CAUSE. Mine was real and unreachable from the declared strategies; the agent found the reachable one.
